episode_title: Avsnitt 100 del 2: Jubileum med tech-oraklet Storm Duncan

insights.quote: Every day when you wake up, the headlines are almost always about tech. What happened to tech? What happened to the subsector of tech? But in my world and the way I see it, tech has now become horizontal. So, every single company has to have a technology sector, a technology focus regardless of which sector they're in.
insights.summary: Technology has evolved from being a vertical sector to a horizontal force that permeates all industries
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

insights.quote: I think those are the companies that don't succeed. And the problem you see is negative contribution margin companies sometimes work out, you know, Uber succeeded even though it was charging less for its product initially to build market share, then it cost them to have that product. But in general, that's not a winning strategy. So most times you can assume that a negative contribution margin business is not going to succeed.
insights.summary: Companies with negative contribution margins rarely succeed, unlike unprofitable companies that reinvest in growth with positive contribution margins
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

insights.quote: You need to figure out what your purpose is in life, right? So for me, I'm in finance, but my purpose is environmental. And so when I'm in finance and I'm out financing companies that I think are going to reduce the consumption of fossil fuels that are going to enhance the quality of our environment for future generations, I'm very comfortable with what I'm doing on a day-to-day basis.
insights.summary: Find your purpose beyond the work itself - for Storm, finance is a tool for environmental impact
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

insights.quote: The quicker you can test your product and the more efficiently and affordably you can test your product with customers and learn from them, the better off you are. So I'd say that's the biggest thing is rapid iterative learning.
insights.summary: Rapid iterative learning and testing hypotheses efficiently is the key to startup success
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

insights.quote: I think one of the things we can appreciate about Amazon and Google, and some of the more successful larger companies, is they've been able to create size and scale and growth while still innovating. So I'd say typically the larger a company gets, the more challenging it is to remain offensive and growth-oriented and innovation-oriented versus defensive in protecting your castle with a moat versus building new castles and conquering new technology lands.
insights.summary: Large companies struggle to balance innovation with defending market position, though Amazon and Google are exceptions
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

insights.quote: I'd say it's focusing on the problem, not the solution, which is core to that learning process. So the more you can focus on what the problem is, as opposed to the solution, the more you're able to dynamically adapt your solution to the problem, as opposed to thinking that you have the one solution to that problem.
insights.summary: Focus on understanding the problem rather than being attached to a specific solution to enable adaptive problem-solving
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

insights.quote: You know, it was actually good luck, I think, more than anything. [...] And at the conclusion, he decided that my advice on what he should do was the best advice. And that was kind of my first appreciation for tech and what it stood for, which was pure meritocrat, you know, sort of meritocratic thinking. So if you had the best ideas, you didn't care how old you were, how experienced you were. It was always the best idea that mattered.
insights.summary: Technology is fundamentally meritocratic - the best ideas win regardless of age or experience
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

insights.quote: if you find your purpose and you always give your clients or your partner the advice that's in their best interest for the long run, you will find that that will over the long run maximize the value of your firm because the profits of a repeat client that is loyal to you are always going to be higher.
insights.summary: Long-term success comes from giving clients advice in their best interest, not focusing on short-term profit
insights.speaker: Storm Duncan

summary: Storm Duncan discusses how technology has become a horizontal force across all industries rather than a standalone sector. The conversation covers M&A strategies (using YouTube/Google and Oracle as examples), the rise of SPACs, key success factors for startups including rapid iterative learning and positive contribution margins, and the future of work as technology displaces employment. No specific stock recommendations were provided, but Duncan emphasized the importance of finding one's purpose beyond just making money.
key_takeaways: Technology is now a horizontal - every company must be tech-first in their vertical
Startup success requires rapid iterative learning, focusing on problems not solutions, and positive contribution margins
Large companies struggle to maintain innovation while defending market position
SPACs give public investors access to earlier stage growth companies but have maturity challenges
Technology will increasingly displace employment, creating societal challenges
